lastPrompt: I want to port this game to Windows. Same features, same graphics, etc. Make a plan for that.

content.thinking: I'm scoping a Windows port of this ~17k-line Swift simulator, which leans heavily on AppKit, SceneKit/Metal, and AVFoundation across ~170 MB of assets and is still under rapid active development. I'll run a parallel inventory of each subsystem's Apple framework dependencies first, then use that to design the port.

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'windows-port-inventory',
  description: 'Inventory every macOS-specific dependency and fidelity-critical feature of the Marvin simulator for a Windows port',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Inventory', detail: '8 parallel readers, one per subsystem' },
    { title: 'Completeness', detail: 'mechanical API sweep against the union of inventories' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/Users/m1/marvin'
const PREAMBLE = `Context: we are planning a port of the Marvin simulator (a native macOS racing/driving game in ${ROOT}/apps/simulator-macos, branch codex/mos-aster-racing-city at commit 1c8bb11) to Windows with the SAME features and the SAME graphics. It is Swift 5.9+/SwiftPM, using AppKit, SceneKit (on Metal), simd, AVFoundation and a little Metal/CoreImage/RealityKit. Targets: SimulationCore (platform-neutral-ish game logic), MarvinSimulator (app, rendering, smoke tests), SimulationChecks (tests). Assets are generated by Python scripts in ${ROOT}/scripts and live under apps/simulator-macos/Resources (and a generated .build/asset-cache).

You are ONE of 8 readers, each inventorying one subsystem. Your output feeds a later design phase that will choose the porting strategy, so be exhaustive and concrete rather than strategic.

Rules:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit files, do not commit, do not build, do not launch the app (other agents are working concurrently).
- The Swift files are very dense (long lines, many statements per line). Read your files IN FULL with the Read tool (use offset/limit for big ones); do not rely on grep alone. Use grep to find cross-references in other files when needed.
- Be concrete: name exact Apple APIs/types/properties (e.g. SCNMaterial.lightingModel = .physicallyBased, SCNShadable.shaderModifiers[.fragment], SCNView.antialiasingMode, AVAudioEnvironmentNode), with file:line references.
- For every platform dependency give realistic Windows options (several where relevant, e.g. D3D12/Vulkan via an engine, Godot, Unity, Unreal, Filament, bgfx, wgpu, SDL3, XAudio2, miniaudio, Steam Audio, etc.) and how hard a faithful port is. Do not pick the overall strategy.
- "Same graphics" is the bar: capture every fidelity-relevant detail (lighting model, shadows incl. map sizes/cascades, AO, MSAA, HDR/tone mapping, fog, sky, custom shader code and what it computes, texture filtering, particle behaviour, camera FOV/motion, post-processing).
- Capture numbers: triangle counts, node/draw-call counts, texture sizes, frame-time budgets, particle limits, audio voice counts, etc., wherever the code or docs state them.
- Note anything that is NOT platform specific and could be reused verbatim (e.g. pure math/game logic), and what tests/smokes/benchmarks validate your subsystem today.
`

const SUBSYSTEMS = [
  { key: 'app-shell-ui', prompt: `Subsystem: APP SHELL, WINDOWING, INPUT, MENUS, HUD, SETTINGS, PERSISTENCE, PACKAGING.
Files: Sources/MarvinSimulator/main.swift, App.swift (all 1159 lines; it also hosts the smoke-test harness - summarize that part briefly, another reader covers validation), SimulatorView.swift, MainMenu.swift, RaceHUD.swift, RaceNavigationMap.swift, FrameRateHUD.swift, LevelLoading.swift, PlayerCharacter.swift, World.swift; Info.plist; build-app.sh; "Launch Marvin.command"; Resources/Icons; README.md sections on the main menu, controls, settings, scores, pause/focus.
Cover: app lifecycle, window/toolbar/menus, keyboard (and any mouse/trackpad/gamepad) input handling and key mapping, how HUD/menus are drawn (AppKit views? SpriteKit overlay? CALayer? SCNView overlay?), fonts used, focus/inactive-window pausing, timing source (CVDisplayLink/SCNSceneRendererDelegate/CACurrentMediaTime), settings persistence (UserDefaults keys), best-score file format/location and atomic writes, command-line flags (list ALL of them), loading screen/progress, app icon handling (light/dark), code signing/packaging.` },
  { key: 'rendering-pipeline', prompt: `Subsystem: RENDERING PIPELINE AND SHADING (the core of "same graphics").
Files: SimulatorView.swift (renderer setup), AOMaterialBinding.swift, AOPreparationProbe.swift, ShadowVolume.swift, TownShadowBatch.swift, BinarySky.swift, FloorGroove.swift, LoadedGPUProbe.swift, BenchmarkGPUCapture.swift, RendererStudy.swift (incl. the RealityKit study), MeshReuseValidation.swift; plus docs/renderer-study.md and docs/apple-gpu-profiling.md in ${ROOT}/docs, and the rendering-related parts of docs/dirt-city.md (search it for MSAA, shadow, SSAO, ambient occlusion, HDR, exposure, bloom, fog, tone).
ALSO: grep ALL of Sources/MarvinSimulator for shaderModifiers, SCNProgram, SCNTechnique, MTL, CIFilter, lightingModel, SCNLight, shadow, wantsHDR, exposure, bloom, screenSpaceAmbientOcclusion, fog, antialiasingMode, lightingEnvironment, background.contents, writesToDepthBuffer, blendMode, renderingOrder, categoryBitMask, SCNLevelOfDetail, SCNGeometrySource, SCNGeometryElement, instancing - and produce a COMPLETE catalogue: every shader modifier (entry point, file:line, what it computes, inputs/uniforms), every light (type, intensity, color temp, shadow settings, map size, cascades, bias), camera settings (FOV, zNear/zFar, HDR, exposure, SSAO params, bloom, motion blur, vignette, color grading), scene fog/background/environment lighting (IBL HDR file), antialiasing, render order/transparency tricks, custom geometry approach, any direct Metal usage. This catalogue is the spec a Windows renderer must match.` },
  { key: 'town-world', prompt: `Subsystem: MOS ASTER TOWN / CITY WORLD (procedural spaceport).
Files: TownWorld.swift (2494 dense lines - read it all), TownGround.swift, TownSigns.swift, TownAccessMap.swift, CityExitWorld.swift, TownDepartureMovie.swift, plus SimulationCore/CityEscape.swift, InfieldLayout.swift, TownEscapeRoute.swift for how they feed geometry; docs/dirt-city.md, docs/dirt-town-plan.md, docs/dirt-town-v1.md; scripts/city/* and Resources/City (what assets are imported vs procedurally generated).
Cover: the procedural generation algorithms (is it deterministic/seeded? what inputs?), the TownMesh / batching approach and how geometry is emitted (SCNGeometrySource layouts, vertex colors, UVs, tangents), material system (CityMaterials etc.: textures, PBR params, shader modifiers), building/prop/people counts, triangle and draw-call counts, LOD/culling, shadow batching, signage/text rendering, spectator crowds geometry, performance budgets and measured frame times in the docs. Identify which parts are pure data/math (portable) vs SceneKit-bound.` },
  { key: 'race-world-effects', prompt: `Subsystem: DIRT TRACK, DESERT, TERRAIN AND EFFECTS.
Files: DirtWorld.swift (765 lines, read all), DesertWorld.swift, DirtTrail.swift, DirtCoating.swift, DeformableSand.swift, WindblownDust.swift, SandstormWorld.swift, TrackBelt.swift, FloorGroove.swift, plus SimulationCore/DirtRace.swift, DesertTerrain.swift, SandDeformation.swift, Sandstorm.swift (only as far as they define the geometry/effects data); docs/dune-sand-contact.md; Resources/Dirt.
Cover: terrain/track mesh generation, brick walls, jumps, materials and textures (Poly Haven dirt etc.), trail/tire-mark rendering (batched meshes, decals?), dirt coating on robots (how is it shaded?), particle systems (SCNParticleSystem or custom? counts, emission rules, sorting, blending), deformable sand (dynamic mesh updates per frame?), windblown dust, sandstorm (fog/volumetrics/visibility changes), binary sky/suns if relevant, dynamic geometry update patterns and their per-frame cost. Identify portable math vs SceneKit-bound code.` },
  { key: 'characters-assets', prompt: `Subsystem: ROBOTS/CHARACTERS, ANIMATION, CROWDS AND THE ASSET PIPELINE.
Files: Robot.swift, R2D2.swift, ImportedRacer.swift, PlayerCharacter.swift, TownCrowd.swift, TownResidents.swift, TownStreetResidents.swift, CitizenMotion.swift, plus SimulationCore/HeadRig.swift, HeadClearance.swift; asset pipeline scripts ${ROOT}/scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py, export-marvin-simulator.py, export-r2d2-simulator.py, export-racers-simulator.py, scripts/city/*; Resources/Marvin, R2D2, BB8, WallE, City (list files, formats, sizes, attribution/licence files); .build/asset-cache contents if present (apps/simulator-macos/.build/asset-cache); docs/town-resident-motion.md.
Cover: runtime model formats (glb? .scn? custom bin+json?) and how they are loaded (SCNScene(url:), ModelIO, custom parser), the CAD-derived Marvin assembly (23 parts, ~695k triangles), how R2-D2/BB-8/WALL-E are imported/converted, articulation/rigging (head pan/tilt, wheels, treads, BB-8 rolling sphere, WALL-E treads) - procedural node transforms vs skinned animation, "acting" poses, crowd/resident animation and instancing, licensing constraints for redistribution on Windows, and whether the Python pipeline itself has macOS-only dependencies (e.g. CAD/STEP tooling, Blender, usdz tools).` },
  { key: 'audio', prompt: `Subsystem: AUDIO.
Files: RaceAudio.swift, RaceVoiceDirector.swift, RaceVoiceChecks.swift, RaceAudioSmoke.swift, any other file using AVFoundation/AudioToolbox (grep); Resources/Audio (formats, counts, sizes, CREDITS.md/Credits.rtf licensing); ${ROOT}/scripts/audio and scripts/make_marvin_robot_voice.sh; docs/race-audio.md and docs/audio-validation/.
Cover: the audio graph (AVAudioEngine nodes, AVAudioEnvironmentNode 3D spatialization, distance attenuation model, reverb, pitch/rate/varispeed for engine sounds, mixing, ducking), how sounds are triggered by game state (overtakes, boosts, crowd, finish, market/cantina ambience, wind/storm), voice direction/phrase variety logic, how audio is synced to the simulation and paused, any TTS (AVSpeechSynthesizer / 'say') at runtime or build time (macOS-only voices would block Windows), and the audio validation/smoke approach. Give Windows options (XAudio2/X3DAudio, WASAPI, miniaudio, OpenAL Soft, FMOD/Wwise, engine-native audio) and what exactly must be replicated for parity.` },

##### rendering-pipeline
All rendering is SceneKit on Metal (benchmark asserts view.renderingAPI == .metal). The shipped game uses no SCNProgram, SCNTechnique, CIFilter or SCNParticleSystem. Every custom effect is a SceneKit shader modifier: a Metal Shading Language snippet injected at the .geometry, .surface or .fragment entry point. Renderer setup lives in App.swift (applicationDidFinishLaunching, startSandbox, startDirtTrack), World.swift (sandbox), MainMenu.swift (portrait view) and DirtWorld.swift plus BinarySky.swift (race and town).

There are three scenes in two SCNViews:
(1) Main-menu portrait: 4x MSAA, LDR. One ambient light and one deferred-shadow directional light. An SCNFloor with an unlit material acts as a shadow catcher.
(2) Sandbox: 4x MSAA, LDR, linear fog from 15 to 38 m. One deferred-shadow sun with a 4096 map fitted to the camera. Flat background colour.
(3) Race, town and dunes:
- 2x MSAA and HDR with fixed exposure.
- Bloom 0.38 / 1.2 / 12 and SceneKit SSAO 0.70 / 1.6 / 0.025.
- Linear fog tinted with the horizon colour: 115 to 240 m clear, 3 to 65 m in a storm.
- A procedural twin-sun sky dome drawn by a fragment modifier.
- Two directional suns, each with its own forward-mode orthographic shadow map (4096 and 2048, 116 m wide). The maps are world-anchored and texel-snapped, not camera-fitted.
- One ambient light, plus image-based lighting from a 64x32 procedural gradient that is regenerated per race.

Materials are mostly .physicallyBased with 2048 scanned maps. sRGB vertex-colour palettes are linearised in shaders with pow 2.2. Ground uses world-space procedural value-noise pigments. Many premultiplied, depth-write-off ground overlays sit millimetres apart.

All geometry is custom SCNGeometry:
- Built once at load: batched town cells with 2 LODs, crowd batches carrying 8 UV channels that drive GPU vertex animation, and dune tiles with 3 LODs.
- Rebuilt every frame: dust and clod particle batches, tread decals and storm grains.

A welded shadow-only proxy mesh is routed into the sun shadow maps through categoryBitMask. Direct Metal is limited to:
- tiny data textures (robot dirt-coating uniforms, dune height deltas)
- one shared MTLBuffer vertex source
- offscreen SCNRenderer diagnostics (LoadedGPUProbe, AOPreparationProbe)
- GPU capture.

RendererStudy is an opt-in RealityKit comparison and does not ship.

The performance target is an M2 MacBook Air at 1920x1080 and 60 Hz. Measured GPU time is about 11.3 to 16 ms per frame with about 2,180 draws, so headroom is tight.
QUANT: Hardware reference: Apple M2 MacBook Air (24 GB), macOS 26.6.2. The drawable is 1920x1080 and the frame budget is 16.67 ms at 60 Hz. Project GPU gate: p99 <= 12.5 ms and maximum < 16.667 ms per minute.

Scene content (10-minute benchmark report):
- Town: 92 cell nodes. 437,850 near / 242,142 far triangles; validate() caps them below 440,000 / 320,000 and fewer than 150 cells.
- 173 exploration cells (51,376 triangles). 497 buildings, 27 signs, 13 streets.
- Crowd: 77 cells, 1,834,674 near / 100,409 far stored triangles. 282 people, of whom 34 walk (up to 10 door residents plus up to 24 street pedestrians).
- Shadow proxies: 92 nodes, 679,992 triangles. Vertices 1,761,272 -> 417,484 and elements 661 -> 338.
- Course surfaces: 5 strips of 768x32 quads, about 245,760 triangles. Desert: 560 tiles of 2,048 triangles at LOD0. Deformable patch: 8,192 triangles each.
- Robots: Marvin 695,172 triangles (plus 112 track-shoe nodes with ribs); R2-D2 25,158; WALL-E 40,158; BB-8 7,166.
- The renderer-study grandstand block alone, with near LOD forced, has 863 meshes and 3,023,194 triangles.

Dynamic effects:
- Debris pool 1,600 particles in 2 draws.
- Storm: 960 particles in 2 draws.
- Trails: 4 racers x up to 128 chunks x 256 marks (up to 131,072 quads). After 10 minutes there were 112,432 quads in 441 nodes before chunking fixes.

Lights and post:
- Lights: 2 directional (shadowed) plus 1 ambient plus IBL.
- Shadow maps 4096 squared and 2048 squared, 116 m wide, 8 PCF samples.
- SSAO pre

##### town-world
Mos Aster is generated entirely in code at level load (DirtWorld.init -> TownWorld(progress:), run on a GCD worker queue in LevelLoading.swift:54-62). Only surface scans (15 Poly Haven 2K JPGs) and the crowd meshes (crowd.json, exported offline from Blender) are imported; every building, street, prop, ground overlay, sign texture and the plaster wear atlas is procedural.

Generation is deterministic: a 64-bit LCG (citySeed 0xA57E2026, TownWorld.swift:532-536) plus integer index hashes drive a fixed call order (roads -> grandstand -> landmarks -> 3 named venues -> settlement -> infield repair pit -> street life -> market/reference details -> wayfinding -> utilities -> doorstep props -> courts -> 130 household yards -> pedestrian access audit -> ground overlays -> activity placement -> 10 doorway residents + 24 street walkers -> crowd batches -> cell geometry). Inputs are the authored street polylines (13 Hermite-smoothed routes), DirtCourse (track spline projection/height, SimulationCore), TownFootprint (irregular radius ~130 m), InfieldLayout and CityExit reservations. The settlement keeps a protected trackside grid core (<56 m), then grows street-facing compounds by frontage placement and 18,000 dart throws with oriented-box SAT separation, then up to 64 small workshops. A 0.25 m BFS flood grid (TownAccessMap, 1320x1320) audits that every compound gets a reachable doorway (up to 6 replanning iterations that shrink blocks). Result at HEAD: 497 buildings, 492/492 accessible compounds, 282 people, 27 signs.

Geometry is emitted by TownPainter primitives (box, adobe rounded prism with wear UVs/damage cavities, cylinder, dome, beam, cable, cloth, arcade, ring, vessel, crate, doors...) into TownMesh CPU buffers that bake vertex colour x contact shading, world-planar UV0 (x0.48) and a wear-atlas UV1, with up to 4 material slots (plaster/cloth/metal/adobe). Each painter call also appends conservative collision bodies (CityCollisionWorld, 8 m buckets) used by physics, residents, camera clipping and route planning. Meshes are welded (exact attribute + guarded tangent-basis key) and uploaded once as SCNGeometry per spatial cell: 92 architecture cells (16 m core / 32 m outer) with a near/far SCNLevelOfDetail at 82 m, plus 173 near-only 16 m exploration-detail cells that fade in (node.opacity) when the player is in the outer town. Per-frame work is limited to toggling cell shadow casting (75 m radius / 48 m race square, optionally frustum-culled shadow volumes), routing those decisions to welded position-only shadow proxies (TownShadowBatch, categoryBitMask bit 20, on by default since db1be0f), exploration fades, crowd uniforms, and resident navigation.

Materials are SceneKit PBR with Metal shader modifiers: vertex sRGB tint linearised with pow 2.2 and modulated by scan luminance; a 1024^2 procedural wear atlas via SCNMaterial.multiply on UV1; transparent premultiplied ground/street overlays whose alpha comes from vertex colour plus world-space value-noise erosion shaders. Spectators are 12 authored human variants x 3 LODs batched into 77 8-m crowd cells, animated entirely in a geometry shader (head turns, waves, gait) driven by 7 extra UV channels and three shared uniforms. Signs are physical frame+plate nodes with text rasterised once through AppKit (Avenir Next Condensed).

##### race-world-effects
DirtWorld (DirtWorld.swift:8) owns one SCNScene for the Dirt Track level. It is constructed on a GCD worker (LevelLoading.swift:55-63), and almost every surface is generated procedurally at load. The race course is a closed periodic cubic B-spline through 16 control points, sampled at 768 points (DirtRace.swift:28-46). The centreline lap is about 136 m and the lane is 3.9 m wide. The elevation function adds a tabletop, rollers, rhythm doubles, a 1.3 m hill, whoops and banking (DirtRace.swift:151-170). From these, courseSurface builds five 768x32 strip meshes: the lane, two berms and two shoulders (DirtWorld.swift:112-126, 435-478). All five share one PBR "clay" material made from the Poly Haven CC0 "dirt" 1K scan, a procedural multiply map and a surface modifier that recolours the clay to rose (DirtWorld.swift:85-108). Other procedural geometry: brick retaining walls batched into two meshes with level bed joints and gate/service cuts (DirtWorld.swift:192-272); heightfield service and city-exit aprons, each with a premultiplied red-clay overlay (DirtWorld.swift:276-372, CityExitWorld.swift:40-85); checker, grid-box and arrow paint; and a baked 768² infield/outfield clay-deposit texture applied in the earth shader in world space (DirtWorld.swift:375-433).

Outside the 156 m town edge, DesertTerrain (SimulationCore) supplies a cached 2 m heightfield. DesertWorld builds 560 static 64 m tiles with crack-free LODs at 0, 130 and 260 m, plus a 4 km horizon plane. TownGround.terrainSurface shades the dune colour, bands and ripple normals in world space. DeformableSand puts opaque 4 m replacement patches (65x65 vertices) where robots touch the dunes. Each patch has a static Metal vertex buffer, and a geometry shader modifier displaces it from an immutable 67x67 R32F height texture that is re-uploaded at 30 Hz from the CPU SandDeformation field. The coarse tile triangles under each patch are removed by rebuilding the tile's index buffer.

Per-frame effects:
- **Tread and tire impressions:** four DirtTrail objects build world-space multiply-blend quads in 256-mark chunks, up to 128 chunk nodes each. They fade in storms through a shader age and distance term.
- **Debris:** a 1,600-slot CPU pool of dust and clods. Its two batched meshes are rebuilt every frame: wind-stretched, view-plane quads with Lambert lighting, and PBR tetrahedra, both premultiplied alpha.
- **Dirt coating on robots:** a geometry-level surface modifier with procedural 3D noise. It is driven by a 2x1 RGBA32F state texture per robot that also carries a dune contact plane.
- **Sandstorm:** about 10% of races. It adds one static drift mesh displaced in the geometry shader by an accumulation uniform, and 960 camera-wrapped grain and haze quads rebuilt per frame. BinarySky switches to dusty linear fog (3-65 m), a muted sky and IBL probe, and suns at 20% intensity.

All weather, deformation, course and terrain maths lives in SimulationCore and is platform-neutral apart from Apple's simd module. All rendering is SceneKit: SCNGeometry, SCNMaterial PBR, shader modifiers written in MSL, LOD, fog, blend modes and rendering order.

##### characters-assets
Each of the four racers is one shared object: Robot (Marvin), R2D2, and ImportedRacer(.bb8/.wallE). All are built at launch in App.swift:103-106 from Bundle.main.resourceURL. The same node trees are reparented between the menu portrait SCNScene, the sandbox World scene and the DirtWorld scene (App.swift:112,458,475-476,517-519; MainMenu.swift:197-202). There are no clones, except in the visual-regression capture.

No model is loaded with SCNScene(url:), ModelIO, glTF, USD or RealityKit. Offline Python converts every source into a custom format, and Swift builds SCNGeometry by hand:
- Marvin: a packed little-endian geometry.bin plus manifest.json. Each part has interleaved float32 position+normal (stride 24) followed by uint32 triangle indices.
- R2-D2, BB-8 and WALL-E: verbose JSON (positions, normals, texcoords, indices, material index, pivots). WALL-E also carries 253 4x4 frames per tread link.
- Crowd: crowd.json holds 12 variants x 3 LODs, with 9 floats per vertex including a semantic surface id.

There is no skinning, morphing, SCNAction, CAAnimation or keyframe playback at runtime. All robot motion is procedural node transforms, set each frame from SimulationCore state (signed left/right track travel, rollingTravel, heading, bodyPitch/bodyRoll or the duneOrientation quaternion, head yaw/pitch, elapsed):
- Marvin: a two-node yaw/pitch neck rig at CAD pivots, gated by an SAT clearance test (HeadClearance). Treads are 56 animated shoes per side on an analytic stadium loop (TrackLoop), plus spinning hub markers and blinking emissive eye strokes.
- R2-D2: three added procedural rollers, and a dome that swivels about an inclined axis.
- BB-8: the shell orientation is integrated as no-slip rolling from ground displacement. The head rides on a mount at the ball centre.
- WALL-E: the authored tread animation is resampled offline into 253 rigid frames per link and scrubbed at runtime by travel/beltLength with lerp+slerp. Gears spin by travel/radius, and the arms are pivot nodes.
- Race "acting" (RacePerformance, pure Swift) outputs a Pose (yaw, pitch, roll, arms, focus) that is added on top of manual input.

Crowds: TownCrowd pre-poses static people on the CPU into 8 m cell batches, with a per-person palette in vertex colours and three LODs. All limb motion (head scans, torso turns, waves, walking gait) runs in a SceneKit .geometry shader modifier (CitizenMotion). It reads per-vertex bind frames and joint weights from seven extra texcoord channels, so it is hand-written GPU rigid-segment deformation. There are 10 doorway visitors (TownResidents) and 24 street walkers (TownStreetResidents). Each is an individual node with its own material copies, whose uniforms (crowdTime, walkCycle, walkBlend) drive a gait based on distance walked. A CPU copy of the same leg transforms (FootPlacement) keeps the soles grounded. Navigation, swept collision, door scheduling and off-screen throttling run on the CPU.

Pipeline: build-app.sh runs prepare-simulator-assets.py, which hash-stamps inputs and outputs in .build/asset-cache and only re-runs exporters when something changed. The three robot exporters use only the Python standard library. Only the offline crowd exporter needs Blender 4.5 LTS (bpy). The shipped crowd.json is committed through Git LFS. Nothing in the pipeline is macOS-only; only the build and packaging shell script is.

##### audio
Race audio is a self-contained, stereo-only sample-playback mixer on AVAudioEngine. AppController.updateRaceAudio (RaceAudio.swift:286-296) drives it once per game tick (60 Hz Timer or CADisplayLink, App.swift:173-180, called at App.swift:445) on the main thread. There is no 3D audio engine: no AVAudioEnvironmentNode, HRTF, reverb, Doppler, occlusion, sidechain or bus ducking. Spatialisation is hand-written 2D math (RaceAudio.spatial/townSpatial). It produces per-source {gain, pan, rate, low-pass cutoff}. The code smooths these with a one-pole filter (75 ms for racer and crowd voices, 650 ms for environment voices) and writes them to AVAudioPlayerNode.volume/.pan, AVAudioUnitVarispeed.rate and a 1-band AVAudioUnitEQ .lowPass.

On first Dirt Track entry, RaceAudio.init (App.swift:488-490, main thread, after the background world build) decodes all 161 bundled WAVs (48 kHz mono PCM16, 51 MB) into 48 kHz stereo float buffers (L=R, about 205 MB). It then builds a fixed graph:
- 30 looping chains: player -> varispeed -> EQ -> bus AVAudioMixerNode.
- 20 one-shot players -> bus.
- bus -> Apple AUPeakLimiter (default parameters) -> mainMixerNode (outputVolume 0.82) -> device.

Each loop slot has a fixed role:
- Per racer slot: low motor, ground contact, high motor, boost hold, sand contact (20 slots).
- 4 crowd slots for the 4 nearest spectator zones.
- Desert wind, market, workshop, cantina, storm gust, storm grit (6 slots).

All loops play continuously from sample 0; silence is gain 0. One-shots use 4 general slots (speech, impact, countdown/go/finish) and 16 critical slots reserved for boost-on/off edges.

Game state drives sound in these ways:
- **Racers:** telemetry (RaceAudio.Actor built from SimulationCore.Simulation: ground speed, track speeds, yaw rate, post-assist throttle/boost/brake, dirt contact, impact serial/speed, off-track sand factor, storm wind/shelter/accumulation) feeds an RPM/load crossfade between low and high motor banks with varispeed pitch, plus surface layers and boost.
- **Edge events:** boost on/off, impacts (>0.65 m/s with a 0.45 s cooldown), countdown beeps, go and finish.
- **Crowds:** the 4 nearest populated spectator zones, scaled by population and storm/finish state, with a 'departed' latch during the post-race escape.
- **Town:** 3 category emitters energy-summed from TownWorld.soundZones. Repair tents use a wall-aware fade.
- **Sandstorm:** two loops whose gain, filter and pan follow the player's local wind vector, shelter and accumulation.
- **Voices:** RaceVoiceDirector (pure logic) emits at most one expression at a time. It greets on first movement, startles on fresh contact, and plays overtake/passed on lap-progress crossings (with hysteresis) within 12 m. Limits: 8 s globally, 22-30 s per robot, 18 s per overtake pair. Six-variant shuffle bags prevent immediate repeats.

The listener stands at the player robot (or at course centre (0,0) after the finish) and faces the camera's yaw.

Sound plays only on the dirt track when not muted, outside the intro, with the window active and visible, and not paused. Otherwise stop() runs (players stopped, engine.pause). Resume reschedules and restarts every loop from sample 0.

There is no TTS at runtime or build time. Voices are pre-rendered offline by Python DSP (a vocoder 'talkbox' over CC-BY effort recordings).

Validation runs offline. --audio-smoke-test uses manual rendering at 800 frames per 1/60 s tick and asserts 61 signal checks. Navigation smoke can capture

##### simulation-core
SimulationCore (20 files, 2,333 lines, 130.8 KB) is a self-contained, almost entirely platform-neutral Swift game-logic library. It has no rendering or UI code. Its parts:
- Simulation (Simulation.swift) is a value-type differential-drive robot. In the sandbox it is kinematic with oriented-footprint obstacle checks. On the dirt track it adds terrain following, ballistic jumps and, when DirtRacePhysics enables robotDynamics, momentum, finite traction, storm drag and a yaw-torque limit. It also handles head yaw/pitch with CAD clearance boxes, track/wheel travel and checkpoints.
- DirtCourse (DirtRace.swift) defines the closed 16-point periodic cubic B-spline circuit: 768 samples, a bounding-volume tree for projection, an analytic elevation/bank/berm/service-ramp height field, and fence projection.
- DirtRace handles countdown, laps and the cooldown lap. DirtScores is a JSON top-10 leaderboard. DirtStandings orders racers.
- DirtRacePhysics is the 240 Hz fixed-step accumulator for all four racers. Each substep advances storm, wind shelter, post-race escape, gate, assists or AI input, each Simulation, the RobotCollisions sequential-impulse solver (24 iterations, plus fence, ground, infield, gate and town solids), CollisionRecovery, and then lap progress.
- DirtOpponent is the AI driver (120 Hz when run standalone). DirtDrivingAssists/DirtRacingLine provide predictive braking and blended steering.
- Sandstorm handles wind, drifts and drag. DesertTerrain is a 769×769 baked dune heightfield. SandDeformation is a 64-tile LRU sand heightfield made of 4 m × 64×64 Float tiles.
- Course entry and exit: CityExit/CityGate (motorised hinge gate), CityCollisionWorld (8 m spatial buckets over about 6,400 town solids), InfieldLayout (seeded salvage and tent fixtures), TownEscapeRoute (grid BFS route planning with line-of-sight simplification and Bézier rounding) and PostRaceEscape (four robots leave through the gate and roam town indefinitely).
- Presentation helpers: RacePerformance (character acting and attention poses), RaceMapRegion/OverviewMotion/TownFootprint (map context and critically damped overview camera), and TrackLoop/HeadRig/HeadClearance (tread belt, neck kinematics, head-to-body separating-axis checks).

All physics is Double precision except the SandDeformation tile storage (Float). The only Apple-only dependency is `import simd` in 13 of the 20 files: about 70 call sites of simd_dot/length/length_squared/distance/normalize/cross plus one simd_quatd/simd_double3x3/.act use. Foundation is used for libm math, and for JSON, files and Date in DirtScores.

The tests (15 files, 1,671 lines) are not XCTest. They are an executable target, SimulationChecks, with an @main runner calling 39 check functions. These use require/near helpers, fputs and exit(1), and take the flags --dunes-only, --escape-only and --assists-only. They check physics invariants, frame-rate independence (10/30/60/120 fps), energy and momentum, geometry seams, and render/collision agreement for the Metal sand snapshot and terrain triangulation. CI (ubuntu) does not run them.

Substantial game logic still lives in the app target, AppController in App.swift:
- the session and race controller: intro/countdown/outro timers, grid shuffle, a 10% storm draw, random daylight, score recording, and pause/focus/occlusion gating;
- the game loop: a 60 Hz Timer with wall-clock dt clamped to 0.1 s for physics, while the race clock uses the unclamped wall delta;
- all camera logic: follow/o

Validation is compiled into the shipping binary. MarvinSimulator scans argv for one of 29 mode flags followed by an output directory (App.swift:90-94, smokeDirectory). 135	Race audio is a self-contained, stereo-only sample-playback mixer on AVAudioEngine. 193	##### simulation-core
194	SimulationCore (20 files, 2,333 lines, 130.8 KB) is a self-contained, almost entirely platform-neutral Swift game-logic library. It has no rendering or UI code. Its parts:
195	- Simulation (Simulation.swift) is a value-type differential-drive robot. In the sandbox it is kinematic with oriented-footprint obstacle checks. On the dirt track it adds terrain following, ballistic jumps and, when DirtRacePhysics enables robotDynamics, momentum, finite traction, storm drag and a yaw-torque limit. It also handles head yaw/pitch with CAD clearance boxes, track/wheel travel and checkpoints.
196	- DirtCourse (DirtRace.swift) defines the closed 16-point periodic cubic B-spline circuit: 768 samples, a bounding-volume tree for projection, an analytic elevation/bank/berm/service-ramp height field, and fence projection.
197	- DirtRace handles countdown, laps and the cooldown lap. DirtScores is a JSON top-10 leaderboard. DirtStandings orders racers.
198	- DirtRacePhysics is the 240 Hz fixed-step accumulator for all four racers. Each substep advances storm, wind shelter, post-race escape, gate, assists or AI input, each Simulation, the RobotCollisions sequential-impulse solver (24 iterations, plus fence, ground, infield, gate and town solids), CollisionRecovery, and then lap progress.
199	- DirtOpponent is the AI driver (120 Hz when run standalone). DirtDrivingAssists/DirtRacingLine provide predictive braking and blended steering.
200	- Sandstorm handles wind, drifts and drag. DesertTerrain is a 769×769 baked dune heightfield. SandDeformation is a 64-tile LRU sand heightfield made of 4 m × 64×64 Float tiles.
201	- Course entry and exit: CityExit/CityGate (motorised hinge gate), CityCollisionWorld (8 m spatial buckets over about 6,400 town solids), InfieldLayout (seeded salvage and tent fixtures), TownEscapeRoute (grid BFS route planning with line-of-sight simplification and Bézier rounding) and PostRaceEscape (four robots leave through the gate and roam town indefinitely).
202	- Presentation helpers: RacePerformance (character acting and attention poses), RaceMapRegion/OverviewMotion/TownFootprint (map context and critically damped overview camera), and TrackLoop/HeadRig/HeadClearance (tread belt, neck kinematics, head-to-body separating-axis checks).
203	
204	All physics is Double precision except the SandDeformation tile storage (Float). The only Apple-only dependency is `import simd` in 13 of the 20 files: about 70 call sites of simd_dot/length/length_squared/distance/normalize/cross plus one simd_quatd/simd_double3x3/.act use. Foundation is used for libm math, and for JSON, files and Date in DirtScores.

##### rendering-pipeline
All rendering is SceneKit on Metal (benchmark asserts view.renderingAPI == .metal). The shipped game uses no SCNProgram, SCNTechnique, CIFilter or SCNParticleSystem. Every custom effect is a SceneKit shader modifier: a Metal Shading Language snippet injected at the .geometry, .surface or .fragment entry point. There are about 20 distinct modifiers, roughly 330 lines of MSL. Note: SimulatorView.swift holds only the input-handling SCNView subclass and the sandbox AppKit HUD. Renderer setup lives in App.swift (applicationDidFinishLaunching, startSandbox, startDirtTrack), World.swift (sandbox), MainMenu.swift (portrait view) and DirtWorld.swift plus BinarySky.swift (race and town).

There are three scenes in two SCNViews:
(1) Main-menu portrait: 4x MSAA, LDR. One ambient light and one deferred-shadow directional light. An SCNFloor with an unlit material acts as a shadow catcher.
(2) Sandbox: 4x MSAA, LDR, linear fog from 15 to 38 m. One deferred-shadow sun with a 4096 map fitted to the camera. Flat background colour.
(3) Race, town and dunes:
- 2x MSAA and HDR with fixed exposure.
- Bloom 0.38 / 1.2 / 12 and SceneKit SSAO 0.70 / 1.6 / 0.025.
- Linear fog tinted with the horizon colour: 115 to 240 m clear, 3 to 65 m in a storm.
- A procedural twin-sun sky dome drawn by a fragment modifier.
- Two directional suns, each with its own forward-mode orthographic shadow map (4096 and 2048, 116 m wide). The maps are world-anchored and texel-snapped, not camera-fitted.
- One ambient light, plus image-based lighting from a 64x32 procedural gradient that is regenerated per race.

Materials are mostly .physicallyBased with 2048 scanned maps. sRGB vertex-colour palettes are linearised in shaders with pow 2.2. Ground uses world-space procedural value-noise pigments. Many premultiplied, depth-write-off ground overlays sit millimetres apart.

All geometry is custom SCNGeometry:
- Built once at load: batched town cells with 2 LODs, crowd batches carrying 8 UV channels that drive GPU vertex animation, and dune tiles with 3 LODs.
- Rebuilt every frame: dust and clod particle batches, tread decals and storm grains.

A welded shadow-only proxy mesh is routed into the sun shadow maps through categoryBitMask. Direct Metal is limited to:
- tiny data textures (robot dirt-coating uniforms, dune height deltas)
- one shared MTLBuffer vertex source
- offscreen SCNRenderer diagnostics (LoadedGPUProbe, AOPreparationProbe)
- GPU capture.

RendererStudy is an opt-in RealityKit comparison and does not ship.

The performance target is an M2 MacBook Air at 1920x1080 and 60 Hz. Measured GPU time is about 11.3 to 16 ms per frame with about 2,180 draws, so headroom is tight.
QUANT: Hardware reference: Apple M2 MacBook Air (24 GB), macOS 26.6.2. The drawable is 1920x1080 and the frame budget is 16.67 ms at 60 Hz. Project GPU gate: p99 <= 12.5 ms and maximum < 16.667 ms per minute.

Scene content (10-minute benchmark report):
- Town: 92 cell nodes. 437,850 near / 242,142 far triangles; validate() caps them below 440,000 / 320,000 and fewer than 150 cells.
- 173 exploration cells (51,376 triangles). 497 buildings, 27 signs, 13 streets.
- Crowd: 77 cells, 1,834,674 near / 100,409 far stored triangles. 282 people, of whom 34 walk (up to 10 door residents plus up to 24 street pedestrians).
- Shadow proxies: 92 nodes, 679,992 triangles. Vertices 1,761,272 -> 417,484 and elements 661 -> 338.
- Course surfaces: 5 strips of 768x32 quads, about 245,760 triangles. Desert: 560 tiles of 2,048 triangles at LOD0. Deformable patch: 8,192 triangles each.
- Robots: Marvin 695,172 triangles (plus 112 track-shoe nodes with ribs); R2-D2 25,158; WALL-E 40,158; BB-8 7,166.
- The renderer-study grandstand block alone, with near LOD forced, has 863 meshes and 3,023,194 triangles.

Dynamic effects:
- Debris pool 1,600 particles in 2 draws.
- Storm: 960 particles in 2 draws.
- Trails: 4 racers x up to 128 chunks x 256 marks (up to 131,072 quads). After 10 minutes there were 112,432 quads in 441 nodes before chunking fixes.

Lights and post:
- Lights: 2 directional (shadowed) plus 1 ambient plus IBL.
- Shadow maps 4096 squared and 2048 squared, 116 m wide, 8 PCF samples.
- SSAO pre

##### town-world
Mos Aster is generated entirely in code at level load (DirtWorld.init -> TownWorld(progress:), run on a GCD worker queue in LevelLoading.swift:54-62). Only surface scans (15 Poly Haven 2K JPGs) and the crowd meshes (crowd.json, exported offline from Blender) are imported; every building, street, prop, ground overlay, sign texture and the plaster wear atlas is procedural.

Generation is deterministic: a 64-bit LCG (citySeed 0xA57E2026, TownWorld.swift:532-536) plus integer index hashes drive a fixed call order (roads -> grandstand -> landmarks -> 3 named venues -> settlement -> infield repair pit -> street life -> market/reference details -> wayfinding -> utilities -> doorstep props -> courts -> 130 household yards -> pedestrian access audit -> ground overlays -> activity placement -> 10 doorway residents + 24 street walkers -> crowd batches -> cell geometry). Inputs are the authored street polylines (13 Hermite-smoothed routes), DirtCourse (track spline projection/height, SimulationCore), TownFootprint (irregular radius ~130 m), InfieldLayout and CityExit reservations. The settlement keeps a protected trackside grid core (<56 m), then grows street-facing compounds by frontage placement and 18,000 dart throws with oriented-box SAT separation, then up to 64 small workshops. A 0.25 m BFS flood grid (TownAccessMap, 1320x1320) audits that every compound gets a reachable doorway (up to 6 replanning iterations that shrink blocks). Result at HEAD: 497 buildings, 492/492 accessible compounds, 282 people, 27 signs.

Geometry is emitted by TownPainter primitives (box, adobe rounded prism with wear UVs/damage cavities, cylinder, dome, beam, cable, cloth, arcade, ring, vessel, crate, doors...) into TownMesh CPU buffers that bake vertex colour x contact shading, world-planar UV0 (x0.48) and a wear-atlas UV1, with up to 4 material slots (plaster/cloth/metal/adobe). Each painter call also appends conservative collision bodies (CityCollisionWorld, 8 m buckets) used by physics, residents, camera clipping and route planning. Meshes are welded (exact attribute + guarded tangent-basis key) and uploaded once as SCNGeometry per spatial cell: 92 architecture cells (16 m core / 32 m outer) with a near/far SCNLevelOfDetail at 82 m, plus 173 near-only 16 m exploration-detail cells that fade in (node.opacity) when the player is in the outer town. Per-frame work is limited to toggling cell shadow casting (75 m radius / 48 m race square, optionally frustum-culled shadow volumes), routing those decisions to welded position-only shadow proxies (TownShadowBatch, categoryBitMask bit 20, on by default since db1be0f), exploration fades, crowd uniforms, and resident navigation.

Materials are SceneKit PBR with Metal shader modifiers: vertex sRGB tint linearised with pow 2.2 and modulated by scan luminance; a 1024^2 procedural wear atlas via SCNMaterial.multiply on UV1; transparent premultiplied ground/street overlays whose alpha comes from vertex colour plus world-space value-noise erosion shaders. Spectators are 12 authored human variants x 3 LODs batched into 77 8-m crowd cells, animated entirely in a geometry shader (head turns, waves, gait) driven by 7 extra UV channels and three shared uniforms. Signs are physical frame+plate nodes with text rasterised once through AppKit (Avenir Next Condensed).
QUANT: Current counts (TownWorld.statistics, recorded in docs/performance-validation/2026-10-03/*.json, matching HEAD's TownWorld since db1be0f): buildings 497 (492 compounds, all accessible; 3 venue routes), streets 13, signs 27 (all text-fit), household yards 130, people 282 (248 batched static + 10 doorway residents + 24 street walkers; 83 grandstand seats), door route connections 24 (~13 physical sliding doors, cap 18), architecture cells 92 (validate < 150), exploration cells 173, crowd cells 77.
Triangles: architecture near 437,850 (budget < 440,000), far 242,142 (budget < 320,000); exploration detail 51,376 (near only); crowd stored near 1,834,674 (budget < 2,100,000), far 100,409 (budget < 115,000), mid LOD ~450k (not counted); per person ~6,500 / 1,600 / 350 (+32 mantle for 1 in 5). Shadow proxies: 92 nodes, 679,992 triangles (near+far), vertices 1,761,272 -> 417,484 position-only, elements 661 -> 338; ~42 active proxies in a typical city-roam frame (caster counts 18-45 across 33 test views). Tangent-key welding removes ~10.4% of town vertices. Street ribbon, ground overlays and brick walls are not in the architecture counters. Collision: ~6,400 town solids (dirt-city.md, earlier layout) in 8 m buckets; access map 1320x1320 Int32 grid at 0.25 m (~7 MB transient), up to 6 replanning iterations; dart throwing 18,000 + 9,000 attempts.
Draws (Xcode replay of a warm production frame, whole scene, all passes, M2): 2,180 draws, 8 render / 4 compute / 67 blit encoders, 17.39 ms rep

##### race-world-effects
DirtWorld (DirtWorld.swift:8) owns one SCNScene for the Dirt Track level. It is constructed on a GCD worker (LevelLoading.swift:55-63), and almost every surface is generated procedurally at load. The race course is a closed periodic cubic B-spline through 16 control points, sampled at 768 points (DirtRace.swift:28-46). The centreline lap is about 136 m and the lane is 3.9 m wide. The elevation function adds a tabletop, rollers, rhythm doubles, a 1.3 m hill, whoops and banking (DirtRace.swift:151-170). From these, courseSurface builds five 768x32 strip meshes: the lane, two berms and two shoulders (DirtWorld.swift:112-126, 435-478). All five share one PBR "clay" material made from the Poly Haven CC0 "dirt" 1K scan, a procedural multiply map and a surface modifier that recolours the clay to rose (DirtWorld.swift:85-108). Other procedural geometry: brick retaining walls batched into two meshes with level bed joints and gate/service cuts (DirtWorld.swift:192-272); heightfield service and city-exit aprons, each with a premultiplied red-clay overlay (DirtWorld.swift:276-372, CityExitWorld.swift:40-85); checker, grid-box and arrow paint; and a baked 768² infield/outfield clay-deposit texture applied in the earth shader in world space (DirtWorld.swift:375-433).

Outside the 156 m town edge, DesertTerrain (SimulationCore) supplies a cached 2 m heightfield. DesertWorld builds 560 static 64 m tiles with crack-free LODs at 0, 130 and 260 m, plus a 4 km horizon plane. TownGround.terrainSurface shades the dune colour, bands and ripple normals in world space. DeformableSand puts opaque 4 m replacement patches (65x65 vertices) where robots touch the dunes. Each patch has a static Metal vertex buffer, and a geometry shader modifier displaces it from an immutable 67x67 R32F height texture that is re-uploaded at 30 Hz from the CPU SandDeformation field. The coarse tile triangles under each patch are removed by rebuilding the tile's index buffer.

Per-frame effects:
- **Tread and tire impressions:** four DirtTrail objects build world-space multiply-blend quads in 256-mark chunks, up to 128 chunk nodes each. They fade in storms through a shader age and distance term.
- **Debris:** a 1,600-slot CPU pool of dust and clods. Its two batched meshes are rebuilt every frame: wind-stretched, view-plane quads with Lambert lighting, and PBR tetrahedra, both premultiplied alpha.
- **Dirt coating on robots:** a geometry-level surface modifier with procedural 3D noise. It is driven by a 2x1 RGBA32F state texture per robot that also carries a dune contact plane.
- **Sandstorm:** about 10% of races. It adds one static drift mesh displaced in the geometry shader by an accumulation uniform, and 960 camera-wrapped grain and haze quads rebuilt per frame. BinarySky switches to dusty linear fog (3-65 m), a muted sky and IBL probe, and suns at 20% intensity.

All weather, deformation, course and terrain maths lives in SimulationCore and is platform-neutral apart from Apple's simd module. All rendering is SceneKit: SCNGeometry, SCNMaterial PBR, shader modifiers written in MSL, LOD, fog, blend modes and rendering order.
QUANT: All counts are computed from the code. Lap, wall and drift figures were estimated with a Python port of the course maths.

Static geometry:
- Course strips: 5 meshes x 49,152 tris = 245,760 tris and 126,885 verts. They cast shadows.
- Lap centreline: about 136.3 m. Inner and outer wall boundaries: about 120.3 m and 152.1 m, i.e. about 280 and 354 brick columns, about 1,900 and 2,600 bricks, roughly 34k and 46k tris (18 tris per brick). That gives 2 draw calls plus shadow passes.
- Service embankment: up to 80x62 cells, about 9.9k tris plus skirt, drawn twice (base and overlay).
- City exit apron: 96x100 cells, 19,200 tris plus about 1.2k skirt, drawn twice.
- Ground plane: 8,192 tris in 2 elements.
- Dune tiles: 560 nodes. Per tile, LOD0 2,048 tris and 1,089 verts; LOD1 696 tris; LOD2 280 tris. LOD0 for all tiles would be 1.15M tris, but zFar 250 m and fog culling limit what is visible.
- Horizon: 1 quad.
- Sky dome: SCNSphere with 48 segments.
- Storm drift mesh: about 9,234 quads, 18.5k tris, 36.9k verts. Hidden when there is no storm.
- Paint: 20 chamfered boxes, 4 grid nodes, 4 arrows.
- Gate: about 20 boxes and 2 cylinders.
- Marvin belts: 2 x (56 shoes + 56 ribs) = 224 small box nodes and 2 x 1,280-tri carcasses. All 112 shoe transforms are updated every frame.

Dynamic geometry:
- Debris: pool of 1,600; at most 440 particles/s (8 contacts x 55/s). 2 draw calls; up to about 6.4k verts (48 B each, about 307 KB) rebuilt every frame.
- Storm particles: 960 quads (880 grain

##### characters-assets
Each of the four racers is one shared object: Robot (Marvin), R2D2, and ImportedRacer(.bb8/.wallE). All are built at launch in App.swift:103-106 from Bundle.main.resourceURL. The same node trees are reparented between the menu portrait SCNScene, the sandbox World scene and the DirtWorld scene (App.swift:112,458,475-476,517-519; MainMenu.swift:197-202). There are no clones, except in the visual-regression capture.

No model is loaded with SCNScene(url:), ModelIO, glTF, USD or RealityKit. Offline Python converts every source into a custom format, and Swift builds SCNGeometry by hand:
- Marvin: a packed little-endian geometry.bin plus manifest.json. Each part has interleaved float32 position+normal (stride 24) followed by uint32 triangle indices.
- R2-D2, BB-8 and WALL-E: verbose JSON (positions, normals, texcoords, indices, material index, pivots). WALL-E also carries 253 4x4 frames per tread link.
- Crowd: crowd.json holds 12 variants x 3 LODs, with 9 floats per vertex including a semantic surface id.

There is no skinning, morphing, SCNAction, CAAnimation or keyframe playback at runtime. All robot motion is procedural node transforms, set each frame from SimulationCore state (signed left/right track travel, rollingTravel, heading, bodyPitch/bodyRoll or the duneOrientation quaternion, head yaw/pitch, elapsed):
- Marvin: a two-node yaw/pitch neck rig at CAD pivots, gated by an SAT clearance test (HeadClearance). Treads are 56 animated shoes per side on an analytic stadium loop (TrackLoop), plus spinning hub markers and blinking emissive eye strokes.
- R2-D2: three added procedural rollers, and a dome that swivels about an inclined axis.
- BB-8: the shell orientation is integrated as no-slip rolling from ground displacement. The head rides on a mount at the ball centre.
- WALL-E: the authored tread animation is resampled offline into 253 rigid frames per link and scrubbed at runtime by travel/beltLength with lerp+slerp. Gears spin by travel/radius, and the arms are pivot nodes.
- Race "acting" (RacePerformance, pure Swift) outputs a Pose (yaw, pitch, roll, arms, focus) that is added on top of manual input.

Crowds: TownCrowd pre-poses static people on the CPU into 8 m cell batches, with a per-person palette in vertex colours and three LODs. All limb motion (head scans, torso turns, waves, walking gait) runs in a SceneKit .geometry shader modifier (CitizenMotion). It reads per-vertex bind frames and joint weights from seven extra texcoord channels, so it is hand-written GPU rigid-segment deformation. There are 10 doorway visitors (TownResidents) and 24 street walkers (TownStreetResidents). Each is an individual node with its own material copies, whose uniforms (crowdTime, walkCycle, walkBlend) drive a gait based on distance walked. A CPU copy of the same leg transforms (FootPlacement) keeps the soles grounded. Navigation, swept collision, door scheduling and off-screen throttling run on the CPU.

Pipeline: build-app.sh runs prepare-simulator-assets.py, which hash-stamps inputs and outputs in .build/asset-cache and only re-runs exporters when something changed. The three robot exporters use only the Python standard library. Only the offline crowd exporter needs Blender 4.5 LTS (bpy). The shipped crowd.json is committed through Git LFS. Nothing in the pipeline is macOS-only; only the build and packaging shell script is.
QUANT: **Triangles**
- Marvin CAD: 695,172 total, 658,415 visible, 343,245 vertices.
- TrackBelt: 2 x 1,280 carcass triangles plus 224 chamfered SceneKit boxes (shoes and ribs).
- R2-D2: 25,158 triangles plus 3 rollers (2 x 48-segment cylinders and 10 spoke boxes each).
- BB-8: 7,166. WALL-E: 40,158.
- The four racers total about 731k triangles of authored mesh, plus generated running gear.

**Nodes and draw calls (per pass, estimated from the code)**
- Marvin: 21 visible CAD nodes (Buttons has 3 elements, so about 23 draws), 2 eyes, 2 x (56 shoes + 56 ribs + 1 carcass) = 226 tread nodes, 4 hubs. About 255 draws; most also cast shadows.
- R2-D2: 14 parts plus 36 wheel sub-nodes, about 50 draws.
- BB-8: 3. WALL-E: 76.
- The robots also get a geometry copy each when DirtCoating installs; there is no instancing.
- Per-frame CPU transforms: 112 shoes, 4 hubs, 2 head nodes, 2 eyes (Marvin); 3 wheels plus dome (R2); ball plus mount (BB-8); 58 links (lerp + slerp), 8 gears, 2 arms, head (WALL-E).

**Crowd**
- 12 variants x 3 LODs (about 6,500 / 1,600 / 350 triangles); 3,571-3,632 LOD0 vertices per variant.
- Budget checked by TownCrowd.valid: modelCount == 12, LOD0 total < 2,100,000 triangles, LOD2 total < 115,000.
- Last documented totals (dirt-city.md): 1,912,586 near, 104,637 far, 77 crowd cells, 294 people.
- README: 298 spectators/residents. Town smoke requires population > 120.
- town-resident-motion.md: 46 conversation groups (96 people), 4 vendor/customer pairs, 7 door waiters, 10 

##### audio
Race audio is a self-contained, stereo-only sample-playback mixer on AVAudioEngine. AppController.updateRaceAudio (RaceAudio.swift:286-296) drives it once per game tick (60 Hz Timer or CADisplayLink, App.swift:173-180, called at App.swift:445) on the main thread. There is no 3D audio engine: no AVAudioEnvironmentNode, HRTF, reverb, Doppler, occlusion, sidechain or bus ducking. Spatialisation is hand-written 2D math (RaceAudio.spatial/townSpatial). It produces per-source {gain, pan, rate, low-pass cutoff}. The code smooths these with a one-pole filter (75 ms for racer and crowd voices, 650 ms for environment voices) and writes them to AVAudioPlayerNode.volume/.pan, AVAudioUnitVarispeed.rate and a 1-band AVAudioUnitEQ .lowPass.

On first Dirt Track entry, RaceAudio.init (App.swift:488-490, main thread, after the background world build) decodes all 161 bundled WAVs (48 kHz mono PCM16, 51 MB) into 48 kHz stereo float buffers (L=R, about 205 MB). It then builds a fixed graph:
- 30 looping chains: player -> varispeed -> EQ -> bus AVAudioMixerNode.
- 20 one-shot players -> bus.
- bus -> Apple AUPeakLimiter (default parameters) -> mainMixerNode (outputVolume 0.82) -> device.

Each loop slot has a fixed role:
- Per racer slot: low motor, ground contact, high motor, boost hold, sand contact (20 slots).
- 4 crowd slots for the 4 nearest spectator zones.
- Desert wind, market, workshop, cantina, storm gust, storm grit (6 slots).

All loops play continuously from sample 0; silence is gain 0. One-shots use 4 general slots (speech, impact, countdown/go/finish) and 16 critical slots reserved for boost-on/off edges.

Game state drives sound in these ways:
- **Racers:** telemetry (RaceAudio.Actor built from SimulationCore.Simulation: ground speed, track speeds, yaw rate, post-assist throttle/boost/brake, dirt contact, impact serial/speed, off-track sand factor, storm wind/shelter/accumulation) feeds an RPM/load crossfade between low and high motor banks with varispeed pitch, plus surface layers and boost.
- **Edge events:** boost on/off, impacts (>0.65 m/s with a 0.45 s cooldown), countdown beeps, go and finish.
- **Crowds:** the 4 nearest populated spectator zones, scaled by population and storm/finish state, with a 'departed' latch during the post-race escape.
- **Town:** 3 category emitters energy-summed from TownWorld.soundZones. Repair tents use a wall-aware fade.
- **Sandstorm:** two loops whose gain, filter and pan follow the player's local wind vector, shelter and accumulation.
- **Voices:** RaceVoiceDirector (pure logic) emits at most one expression at a time. It greets on first movement, startles on fresh contact, and plays overtake/passed on lap-progress crossings (with hysteresis) within 12 m. Limits: 8 s globally, 22-30 s per robot, 18 s per overtake pair. Six-variant shuffle bags prevent immediate repeats.

The listener stands at the player robot (or at course centre (0,0) after the finish) and faces the camera's yaw.

Sound plays only on the dirt track when not muted, outside the intro, with the window active and visible, and not paused. Otherwise stop() runs (players stopped, engine.pause). Resume reschedules and restarts every loop from sample 0.

There is no TTS at runtime or build time. Voices are pre-rendered offline by Python DSP (a vocoder 'talkbox' over CC-BY effort recordings).

Validation runs offline. --audio-smoke-test uses manual rendering at 800 frames per 1/60 s tick and asserts 61 signal checks. Navigation smoke can capture
QUANT: **Voices and graph.**
- 30 permanently running loop voices plus 20 one-shot slots (4 general, 16 critical) = 50 maximum simultaneous sources.
- About 114 AVAudioNodes: 30 players, 30 varispeeds, 30 EQs, 20 shot players, bus, limiter, main mixer and output.
- Limiter: lookahead latency 96 samples (2 ms). Varispeed chain latency: about 8 samples.
- At most 1 speech clip at a time.

**Memory and decode.**
- 161 assets loaded; 51.3 MB on disk; 205.36 MB decoded as stereo float.
- Mono int16 would need 51 MB, mono float 103 MB.
- Decoding happens synchronously on the main thread at the first startDirtTrack; it was not timed.

**Update cadence.**
- 60 Hz with dt clamped to 0.1 s.
- Offline: 800 frames per tick (1024 maximum).
- Smoothing tau: 75 ms for racers and crowd, 650 ms for environment.
- Measured internal mixer ramps: volume about 1200 frames (25 ms), pan about 1080 frames.

**Rates and pitch.**
- Low motor 0.66-1.38; high 0.75-1.37; boost 0.85-1.20; ground 0.65-1.50; sand 0.75-1.15; crowd 1.0-1.057; storm gust 0.8-1.08; grit 0.9-1.06.

**Ranges.**
- Racers 36 m, crowd 32 m, town 32 m (workshop 26 m, repair tents 14 m), speech 14 m.
- The voice director's near radius is 12 m.
- Spatial reference distance is 6 m (repair-tent proximity scale 2.5 m). Cutoff floor is 1400 Hz for positional sources and 900 Hz for storm gust.

**Speech budget.**
- Global gap 8 s; per robot 22-30 s; per overtake pair 18 s; pending entries expire after 2 s.
- Test limits: at most 1 event in 10 min 

##### simulation-core
SimulationCore (20 files, 2,333 lines, 130.8 KB) is a self-contained, almost entirely platform-neutral Swift game-logic library. It has no rendering or UI code. Its parts:
- Simulation (Simulation.swift) is a value-type differential-drive robot. In the sandbox it is kinematic with oriented-footprint obstacle checks. On the dirt track it adds terrain following, ballistic jumps and, when DirtRacePhysics enables robotDynamics, momentum, finite traction, storm drag and a yaw-torque limit. It also handles head yaw/pitch with CAD clearance boxes, track/wheel travel and checkpoints.
- DirtCourse (DirtRace.swift) defines the closed 16-point periodic cubic B-spline circuit: 768 samples, a bounding-volume tree for projection, an analytic elevation/bank/berm/service-ramp height field, and fence projection.
- DirtRace handles countdown, laps and the cooldown lap. DirtScores is a JSON top-10 leaderboard. DirtStandings orders racers.
- DirtRacePhysics is the 240 Hz fixed-step accumulator for all four racers. Each substep advances storm, wind shelter, post-race escape, gate, assists or AI input, each Simulation, the RobotCollisions sequential-impulse solver (24 iterations, plus fence, ground, infield, gate and town solids), CollisionRecovery, and then lap progress.
- DirtOpponent is the AI driver (120 Hz when run standalone). DirtDrivingAssists/DirtRacingLine provide predictive braking and blended steering.
- Sandstorm handles wind, drifts and drag. DesertTerrain is a 769×769 baked dune heightfield. SandDeformation is a 64-tile LRU sand heightfield made of 4 m × 64×64 Float tiles.
- Course entry and exit: CityExit/CityGate (motorised hinge gate), CityCollisionWorld (8 m spatial buckets over about 6,400 town solids), InfieldLayout (seeded salvage and tent fixtures), TownEscapeRoute (grid BFS route planning with line-of-sight simplification and Bézier rounding) and PostRaceEscape (four robots leave through the gate and roam town indefinitely).
- Presentation helpers: RacePerformance (character acting and attention poses), RaceMapRegion/OverviewMotion/TownFootprint (map context and critically damped overview camera), and TrackLoop/HeadRig/HeadClearance (tread belt, neck kinematics, head-to-body separating-axis checks).

All physics is Double precision except the SandDeformation tile storage (Float). The only Apple-only dependency is `import simd` in 13 of the 20 files: about 70 call sites of simd_dot/length/length_squared/distance/normalize/cross plus one simd_quatd/simd_double3x3/.act use. Foundation is used for libm math, and for JSON, files and Date in DirtScores.

   Seen as a graphics engineer, "same graphics as SceneKit" is a renderer-semantics problem. Both custom-renderer plans solve it at the root. The Godot plan has to reach the same semantics through engine extension points that verifiably fall short.

Where Godot falls short:
- With MSAA on, only POST_TRANSPARENT CompositorEffects run (godot#106743), so a custom AO pass before lighting is impossible.
- Linear tonemap clips, and the colour-correction LUT is applied after tonemapping, so the Level-0/1 tone plan cannot work.
- Directional shadows are split evenly in the atlas and fitted to the camera frustum (verified in renderer_scene_cull.cpp and light_storage.cpp), so world-anchored 4096/2048 parity needs an engine fork.
- SwiftGodot on Windows is a source build with unverified stability.

Between the two custom renderers, the incremental plan has essentially the same fidelity machinery as the own-renderer plan:
- same-process dual render on the M2;
- a term-by-term characterisation suite;
- shader-stage order reproduced deliberately;
- geometry effects in every pass;
- primitives exported from SceneKit.

It carries less technical risk:
- bgfx's D3D11 path is mature, with offline-compil

Four things set it apart.\n\n1. **It reduces risk early and visibly.** SimulationChecks run on Windows CI in week 1, and a Swift+bgfx+SDL3 build captures a PNG on a WARP runner before any hardware is bought. A playable Windows sandbox follows around week 4 and a race around week 7, each with a go/no-go gate and a stated fallback.\n\n2. **Sync is enforced by mechanism, not diligence.**\n- Compiler-checked module boundaries, plus a Linux CI build.\n- Exhaustive feature enums with an explicit .parityDebt escape hatch.\n- Shared effect sources that generate both the SceneKit MSL and the bgfx shaders.\n- Same-commit goldens.\n- A 72-hour debt SLA.\n- A quantified steady-state cost: 0.3-0.5 FTE while both renderers exist, then 0.1-0.2 FTE.\n\n3. **It fits the user's standing rules and the agent workflow.**\n- Agents keep working and committing from the Mac, so Entire provenance and Astra review are unchanged.\n- Visual cal
CRIT verdict Revise before approval. Most of the plan's technology claims hold up when checked on the web: SDL 3.4.18 (2026-10-02), Godot 4.7.2, godot#106743 (still open), SDL #11696 (milestone 3.6.0), Swift 6.4 released 2026-09-15 with Swift Build as the default, SE-0482 limited to C libraries, D3D11 feature level 11_0 mandating 4x/8x MSAA but not 2x, PresentMon --v2_metrics, Artifact Signing at $9.99 with its eligibility rules, the UserDefaults path on Windows, and the SwiftGodot README. Its codebase facts also check out: 80 commits at 6/7/2/4/15/15/17/14 per day, one author, App.swift touched by 49 of them, 39 SimulationChecks, 61 audio checks, and 161 dependencies (87 low, 54 medium, 17 high, 3 very high) plus 246 fidelity rows, matching inventory.json. Six major problems remain. (1) The Windows performance gate and per-pass budgets contradict SceneKit's measured costs and contradict each other. (2) The parity-debt rule would throttle the Mac line the plan promises to protect. (3) The VecMath design breaks layout-hash identity, because the town generator's thresholds run through simd_* calls, not only libm. (4) The staffing arithmetic does not support 23 weeks. (5) The legal scope leaves out character copyright and model provenance. (6) The parity thresholds have no coherent calibration basis. There are also 11 minor errors, inconsistencies and gaps.

A portable presentation backend follows: SDL3, bgfx (D3D11 on Windows, Metal on the Mac), Blend2D, and PortableMixer on miniaudio. It is developed mostly inside the Mac app against SceneKit at the same commit. SceneKit stays the Mac default; moving the Mac to bgfx-Metal is decided at G4. Fallbacks: SDL_gpu or wgpu behind the RenderScene port, then Godot plus a C-ABI presenter at G2.

Appendix C collects these. 18 - Appendix A corrects claims made in the proposals. Appendix D lists what changed in response to the review. 19 20 **Velocity, checked in git:** 21 - 80 simulator commits since 2026-09-26, at 6, 7, 2, 4, 15, 15, 17 and 14 per day. All have one human author, who directs agents. 22 - 61 of the 80 touched render, scene or HUD files. 42 changed shader-modifier or material text. 36 touched SimulationCore. 23 - Hot files: App.swift was touched by 49 commits, TownWorld.swift by 27, DirtWorld.swift by 25 and TownSmoke.swift by 25. 24 25 --- 26 27 ## 1. Goal and scope 28 29 ### 1.1 Goal 30 31 Ship a native Windows build of Marvin Simulator with the same features and the same graphics as the macOS SceneKit build at the same commit. The Mac game must keep shipping and developing at 10-17 agent commits a day. 32 33 **Supported Windows versions:** 34 - Windows 11 x64, version 25H2 or later. The reference and benchmark machines run 25H2. 35 - 24H2 is a compatibility test only. Home and Pro servicing ends on 2026-10-13; Enterprise and Education servicing ends on 2027-10-12 [S42]. 36 - 23H2 is unsupported. Home and Pro servicing ended on 2025-11-11 [S42]. 37 - Windows 10 is not tested. ARM64 is optional (§11). 38 39 There is no compatibility-layer shortcut. SceneKit, AppKit, AVFoundation and Apple's `simd` module have no Windows implementation, so the port has to be done at source level. 40 41 ### 1.2 What "same features" means operationally 42 43 **Feature checklist.** `parity/feature-checklist.json` is generated from `inventory.json`. It holds all 246 fidelity-spec rows: 241 from the readers and 5 from the critic. Each row ends either implemented and verified (by a named test or capture) or waived by you. Gate G3 requires 100%. 44 45 **User-visible scope:** 46 - **Main menu:** live 3D portrait of the 4 robots, the hidden B/R/W/M letters and the 6 persisted settings. 47 - **Sandbox.** 48 - **Race:** the 3-lap Dirt Track with 4 racers, AI, assists and robot collisions. 49 - **Weather and light:** a 10% sandstorm chance per race and per reset, and twin-sun daylight. 50 - **Mos Aster town:** 51 - 497 buildings, 282 people, 27 signs and 13 streets; 52 - 92 + 173 cells with LOD and exploration fades; 53 - residents, street walkers and sliding doors. 54 - **Track surroundings:** the gate (G key), the apron and the city exit. 55 - **Terrain effects:** dunes with deformable sand, trails, debris and robot coating. 56 - **Post-race:** escape into town and roaming. 57 - **Navigation and cameras:** COURSE/TOWN/DUNES maps, camera modes and intro/outro flights. 58 - **Screens:** HUDs, FPS readout, loading screen, scores, pause and focus semantics, and mute. 59 - **Audio:** 30 loop voices, 20 one-shot slots and the voice lines. 60 - **Input:** keyboard and mouse. 61 62 **Behaviour parity is tolerance-based, not bit-identical.** 63 - libm and FMA differ between platforms, and the 4-robot race is chaotic: its totals already span 90.3-101.5 s across frame rates. 64 - The 39 SimulationChecks must pass on Windows. 65 - A tolerance may change only with your recorded approval and a root-cause note (G0). The known candidate is the coupled-race spread limit: 12 s, against a recorded 11.16 s. 66 - Long runs are compared statistically. 67 68 **Developer contract.** These stay the same, so `check-sustained-performance.py`, the docs and `docs/simulator-agent-rules.md` §10 keep working: 69 - the smoke and benchmark flags (63, minus the Apple-only diagnostics in §1.4); 70 - the ~23 `MARVIN_*` variables; 71 - output-directory semantics, exit codes and JSON schemas. 72 73 ### 1.3 What "same graphics" means operationally 74 75 1. **Identical inputs by construction.** 76 - Geometry, procedural textures, material parameters, camera maths and simulation state all come from the same Swift generators, seeds and assets. 77 - The town layout hash must be equal on macOS, Linux and Windows. That covers both vector maths and transcendental functions (§4.1). Otherwise you approve an alternative (§11). 78 2. **Identical render configuration.** 79 - **Race:** 80 - 1920x1080 with 2x MSAA; two shadowed suns with world-anchored, texel-snapped 4096/2048 maps 116 m wide. 81 - SSAO 0.70/1.6/0.025, HDR with fixed exposure, and bloom 0.38/1.2/12. 82 - Linear fog: 115-240 m clear, 3-65 m in a storm. 83 - A procedural sky plus a 64x32 IBL probe. 84 - LOD switches at 8/10/24/26/82/130/260 m. 85 - Reverse-Z with the near plane at 0.02 m. 86 - **Sandbox and menu:** LDR with 4x MSAA, one deferred-shadow light each, and SceneKit's automatic shadow-projection fit (characterised in §5.2). The sandbox has fog at 15-38 m. 87 3. **Measured shading parity** against SceneKit renders of a frozen scenario table at the same commit: 88 - metrics are object-ID coverage, FLIP, ΔE00 and SSIM per region; 89 - thresholds come from measured noise floors (§5.5). 90 4. **Human acceptance per area**, as the rules require. You and the Astra judge review contact sheets and motion side-by-sides. A passing metric is never acceptance. 91 92 **Deviations agreed in advance (each needs your yes in §11):** 93 - **Fonts.** SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next cannot ship [S28][S30], so the HUD layout is re-baselined after the font switch (§5.5). 94 - **OS chrome.** 95 - **Display colour management and HDR.** macOS ColorSync versus Windows SDR sRGB and Windows HDR mode. Parity is judged on captures (§5.7). 96 - **GPU-vendor differences.** `fract(sin)` noise, MSAA sample positions, anisotropic filtering and fp16 handling (§5.3, §5.5). 97 98 ### 1.4 Out of scope 99 100 | Item | Why it is out of scope | 101 |---|---| 102 | RealityKit renderer study (`--renderer-study`, `--realitykit`, RendererStudy.swift, 333 lines) | An Apple-only migration experiment; it does not ship. | 103 | SceneKit shader-string GPU probes: LoadedGPUProbe (252), AOPreparationProbe (148), AOMaterialBinding (77), BenchmarkGPUCapture (39) | They depend on SceneKit modifier-text surgery and owned Metal command buffers. Replaced by per-view GPU timers, scene-feature toggles (ABBA variants become flags), RenderDoc/PIX and PresentMon. Flags keep their names where the meaning survives. | 104 | AO fixtures (AOPreparationFixture, GroundTruthAOFixture with CryptoKit, experimental GTAO) | Mac research tools. GTAO stays an analytic reference. | 105 | Display-link diagnostics, and the CAMetalLayer presentation-calibration app | Apple pacing paths. `--display-link-lifecycle-check` becomes `--lifecycle-check` with the same checks. | 106 | Gamepad | The Mac build has none. | 107 | New features; fixing the Mac's failing 10-minute 60 fps gate | The port is a parity project. The Windows gate is defined in §8.2. | 108 | Translucent title bar; native Win32 menu bar | OS chrome. A Win32 menu also brings modal-loop and Alt/F10 problems. | 109 | Microsoft Store, Steam, public release | They wait for legal review of four things: character copyright and trademarks (Lucasfilm/Disney, Pixar); provenance of the robot models obtained from mirrors; CERN-OHL-S-2.0 obligations; and reimplementing maths read from captures (§9). | 110 | Pixel-identical text to SF fonts; bit-identical physics traces across OSes | Impossible because of licensing and libm. Replaced by layout and statistical parity. | 111 | Windows UI Automation for the custom-drawn menu | SDL does not provide it. Decision item; the default is a later follow-up. | 112 113 --- 114 115 ## 2. Recommendation 116 117 ### 2.1 Chosen strategy: seams first, same source 118 119 Make the Swift game portable on the live Mac line. Then add a second, portable presentation backend that renders the same engine-neutral scene data. 120 121 **Step 1: extract the game from SceneKit and AppKit.** 122 - Small, behaviour-neutral, codemod-generated PRs move game logic and world construction out of SceneKit and AppKit: 123 - about 2,100 lines into **GameCore**; 124 - about 3,900 lines into **WorldBuild**. 125 - They sit behind six narrow ports: RenderScene, Canvas2D, AudioOut, PlatformShell, Storage and TestHost. 126 - Each PR must leave Mac SceneKit captures unchanged within the measured noise floor. 127 128 **Step 2: build the portable backend:** 129 - **SDL3 3.4.x** for windowing and input [S12]; 130 - **bgfx** for rendering: Direct3D 11 on Windows, Metal on the Mac, Vulkan as secondary [S1]; 131 - **Blend2D** for HUD and sign text [S15]; 132 - **PortableMixer**, a small C mixer, on miniaudio 0.11.x [S16]. 133 134 **Where the work happens.** The portable backend also runs inside the Mac app behind `--renderer bgfx`. • Diligent's Metal backend is commercial-licence only [S41].
